rule: a claim stands as stated iff it holds in >= 10 of 11 census runs under every variant (variant_a, variant_b, variant_c, variant_abc); applied to both threshold sets (dedup_stored, a_alive_pooled); clean lanes reported alongside

claims.c1_order_com: census COM ordering Tg < Ab < Di
claims.c2_persist: mean lineage lifespan Tg > Di and Ab > Di (Fig. 4a records; both ratios > 1)
claims.c3_rise_fall: superclass census rises and falls (interior argmax and last <= 0.8 x max)

notes: variant_a is near-degenerate: the pooled label-free SAI null p95 is 0.998 (ViT, CCT) and 0.9998 (ResNet), because shuffled SAI of dense features approaches 1; only 0-4 lineage records per run (of thousands) and ~0.1% of alive census features at the first checkpoint exceed it. variant_a failures of claims 1 and 2 are therefore the task-general category emptying, not a reordering of existing task-general features; the superclass parts (COM Ab < Di, lifespan Ab > Di) hold in >= 10/11 runs under every variant.

VitSmall seed 256 has a 1536-feature dictionary (768 in the other ViTs); under the 10%-of-dictionary rule all six of its layers are unhealthy (median alive 6.7-8.8%), so it is not evaluable under variant_c / variant_abc.
